attachments.name: Safran Sole Source Justification
attachments.text:
MISSOULA COUNTY
"SOLE SOURCE" JUSTIFICATION
Section 10D of the Missoula County Purchasing and Contracts Policy allows a contract to be awarded for a supply or service item
without competition under certain circumstances. The required item must be available only from a single supplier. Circumstances
which could necessitate a sole source procurement are: (1) only one vendor can provide services, equipment, accessories, or
replacement parts compatible with County requirements ; (2) no other equivalent product exists; or (3) only one source is acceptable
or suitable for the supply or service item. Sole source procedures do not apply if the item is under $5,000.
Department name: OEM
1. Name of product or service: GPS Master Oscillator
2. Name of product manufacturer: Safran
3. Name of "sole" product supplier or service provider: Safran
4. What evaluation of other product suppliers or service providers was made? (Please furnish
names, addresses, and other documentation.)
We did not look at other options since we currently use the Safran SecureSync GPS at our radio
sites. We are adding a second unit to each radio site for redundancy and to provide enough
reference outputs for the transmitters we will be replacing this summer. From a maintenance,
configuration and spare parts perspective we feel it is best to continue using the Safran
SecureSync units.
5. What makes this particular product or service unique and unavailable from other sources?
We currently use this equipment and it provides the outputs we need.
6. How did you determine that there was only one source for the product or service?
Ordering direct from the manufacturer.
7. What product supplier or service provider has your Department used until now to satisfy similar
requirements?
We have been using Safran (formally Orolia, formally Spectracom) for our simulcast timing since
the early 2000’s
8. Attach dated quote.

matters.title: Request board approve chair to sign agreement between UM Forestry Program and Missoula County (OEM) for sharing resources in prescribed fire efforts.
matters.text: Requesting the board chair sign an agreement between University of Montana and Missoula County(OEM-Wildfire Mitigation Program) to share resources to accomplish prescribed fire objectives on Missoula County and University of Montana lands. This is an agreement to share resources, knowledge, and experience. There will be no exchange of financial resources.

attachments.name: OEM_MSO_County_NCLFA_MOU_County Final_VH_ECM
attachments.text:
COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT
BETWEEN
MISSOULA COUNTY OFFICE OF EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT
AND
MONTANA FOREST AND CONSERVATION EXPERIMENT STATION
AND
NATIONAL CENTER FOR LANDSCAPE FIRE ANALYSIS
This Cooperative Agreement (CA), between Missoula County Office of Emergency Management,
hereinafter referred to as “OEM,” and the Montana Forest and Conservation Experiment Station of the
W.A. Franke College of Forestry and Conservation, hereinafter referred to as “MFCES,” and the
National Center for Landscape Fire Analysis at the University of Montana, hereinafter referred to as
“NCLFA” is for cooperative planning, implementation, and research of prescribed burning on
properties owned and managed by MFCES and Missoula County. OEM, MFCES, and the NCLFA
shall be referred to individually as “Party” and collectively as “Parties”.
1. Background
Missoula County Office of Emergency Management coordinates Fire/Fuel management activities
on Missoula County and Private Lands, to educate, and assist in reducing the risk of Wildfire
damage by starting with the Home Ignition Zone (HIZ) and moving outward and working together
with neighborhoods to make communities safer.
MFCES’s mission is to conduct research in forest management that helps society to sustainably
manage its natural resources, and to train and educate students, professionals, civil servants, and
the general public. MFCES owns and manages fire-dependent lands that contain a diversity of
plants, animals, and habitats.
The National Center for Landscape Fire Analysis (NCLFA) plans, implements, conducts research,
and provides training and education on prescribed fires. The FireCenter leads and manages fire
activities on MFCES properties and supports fire activities on partner lands.
2. Purpose
The purpose of this CA is to document the cooperation between the Parties in the planning,
implementation, and research of prescribed fire and fuels management on Missoula County lands
and MFCES lands, in accordance with the following provisions.
Page 1 of 4
3. Responsibilities
a) Missoula County will:
i) Provide a project manager to work with the assigned NCLFA project manager.
ii) Maintain responsibility and oversight for activities on Missoula County lands.
iii) Develop burn plans (including developing objectives) and provide the final decision on
whether to proceed with a prescribed fire on Missoula County lands.
iv) Contribute equipment and personnel to burn planning and implementation as resources
allow.
v) Provide orientation, maps, and gate keys as necessary for the project area/s for which the
work under this CA will be performed.
b) MFCES will:
i) Provide forest management objectives for MFCES properties.
ii) Provide expertise in forest management.
iii) Provide equipment and personnel as resources allow.
c) NCLFA will:
i) Provide a project manager to work with the assigned OEM project manager.
ii) Review Missoula County burn plans and provide insight and expertise as needed during
development.
iii) Contribute equipment and personnel to burn planning and implementation as resources
allow.
iv) Provide orientation, maps, and gate keys as necessary for the project areas for which the
work under this CA will be performed.
v) Provide NWCG and other training when needed and appropriate.
vi) Utilize Unmanned Aerial Systems for data collection and aerial ignitions when appropriate.
d) NCLFA, MFCES, and OEM will:
i) Coordinate project activities through the project managers.
ii) Periodically review the CA and cooperatively recommend changes, which will be
memorialized in writing as an amendment to this CA.
iii) Provide access to pertinent files and plans upon request from the other Party.
4. It is mutually agreed:
a) Upon request, personnel and equipment may be temporarily provided by the Parties to each
other pursuant to the terms and conditions outlined in this CA. Provision of personnel and
equipment shall be provided at the sole discretion of each individual Party, based partially upon
workloads, priorities, and availability of resources. Personnel and equipment provided under
this CA may be used for, but are not limited to, the following purposes:
Page 2 of 4
i) Technical assistance, including preparation or review of site or landscape-level fire
management plans and prescribed fire unit plans (“burn plans”), forest and other
management plans, inventories, and analysis.
ii) Pre-burn preparations include vegetation and fuel load sampling, control line construction
and maintenance, environmental monitoring, and fuels manipulation.
iii) Burn implementation, including project supervision, ignition, holding, fire behavior, and
weather monitoring, logistical support, and mop-up.
iv) Post-burn monitoring and evaluation.
v) Research conducted pre-, during, and post-fire.
b) For each prescribed burn, the responsible Party shall complete a burn plan. The formality of the
burn plan shall be governed by the risks and scope of the intended prescribed burn.
c) The Parties shall designate a burn boss, who will be responsible for supervising a prescribed
fire in accordance with the burn plan.
d) Each Party shall be financially responsible for its own personnel, costs, and equipment. Unless
expressly agreed to in a written amendment to this CA, each Party shall pay all salaries,
benefits, and obligations owed to its own personnel and shall cover the costs of operation and
maintenance of its own equipment, and there shall be no exchange of funds for the obligations
described herein.
e) Changes to this CA must be agreed to via a written amendment signed by both Parties.
f) This CA may be terminated if either Party, due to overriding circumstances, is unable to fulfill
its obligations. If a Party wishes to terminate the CA, they must provide written notice 30 days
in advance to the other Party.
g) This CA is not assignable.
h) Nothing in this CA is intended to waive or otherwise limit any applicable law, rule, regulation,
or any other requirements or duties under such laws, rules, or regulations.
5. Scope and Duration
This CA is effective upon the date of the last signature below and will expire on December 31,
2030, unless extended via written amendment signed by both Parties.
